title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 2.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 2, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth
I made me gardens and orchards
I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine
I gathered me also silver and gold
questions.correctAnswer: I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in Ecclesiastes 2:1.

questions.question: What did the speaker say of laughter in Ecclesiastes 2:2?
questions.explanation: The speaker explicitly states in Ecclesiastes 2:2, 'I said of laughter, It is mad'.

questions.question: What did the speaker seek to give himself unto in Ecclesiastes 2:3?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:3 states, 'I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine'.

questions.question: What did the speaker build according to Ecclesiastes 2:4?
questions.explanation: The verse Ecclesiastes 2:4 mentions that the speaker built houses and planted vineyards.

questions.question: What kind of trees did the speaker plant in Ecclesiastes 2:5?
options: Trees of all kind of fruits
questions.correctAnswer: Trees of all kind of fruits
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:5 states, 'I planted trees in them of all kind of fruits'.

questions.question: What did the speaker make pools of in Ecclesiastes 2:6?
questions.explanation: The text in Ecclesiastes 2:6 states, 'I made me pools of water'.

questions.question: What did the speaker have born in his house according to Ecclesiastes 2:7?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:7 mentions that the speaker had 'servants born in my house'.

questions.question: What kind of possessions did the speaker have above all in Jerusalem according to Ecclesiastes 2:7?
options: Great possessions of great and small cattle
questions.correctAnswer: Great possessions of great and small cattle
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:7 states, 'I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me'.

questions.question: What did the speaker gather in Ecclesiastes 2:8?
questions.explanation: The verse Ecclesiastes 2:8 mentions that the speaker gathered silver, gold, and musical instruments.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:9, how did the speaker compare to those before him in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:9 states, 'So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem'.

questions.question: Did the speaker's wisdom remain with him according to Ecclesiastes 2:9?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:9 confirms, 'also my wisdom remained with me'.

questions.question: True or False: The speaker sought to understand what was good for the sons of men.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:3 states that the speaker sought to see what was good for the sons of men.

questions.question: True or False: The speaker built a temple in Ecclesiastes 2.
questions.explanation: While not explicitly mentioned, the speaker made great works, implying significant construction, such as houses.

questions.question: True or False: The speaker claimed to have no possessions in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:7 states that the speaker had great possessions, contradicting the claim of having none.

questions.question: True or False: The speaker had only male servants according to Ecclesiastes 2:7.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:7 mentions both servants and maidens, indicating both genders.

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the author keep from his eyes according to Ecclesiastes 2:10?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them,' which means the author indulged in all his desires.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 2:11 promise will happen if someone looks upon their works?
questions.explanation: According to Ecclesiastes 2:11, looking upon all the works leads to the realization that 'all was vanity and vexation of spirit.'

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:12, what is compared in the author's observation?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:12 mentions the author turning to 'behold wisdom, and madness, and folly,' indicating his contemplation of these concepts.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 2:13 reveal about wisdom compared to folly?
options: Folly is more enjoyable than wisdom
questions.explanation: In Ecclesiastes 2:13, it clearly states 'Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly,' highlighting the superiority of wisdom.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:14, what does the wise man's eyes allow him to do?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The wise man's eyes are in his head,' suggesting that wisdom allows for perception and understanding.

questions.question: What realization does the author come to in Ecclesiastes 2:15 regarding wisdom?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:15 states, 'Then I said in my heart, that this also is vanity,' indicating the author's conclusion about wisdom.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:16, how is the remembrance of the wise compared to the fool?
options: The wise man's legacy is greater
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'for there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever,' indicating that both will ultimately be forgotten.

questions.question: What did the author express about life in Ecclesiastes 2:17?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:17 states, 'Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me,' showing his disdain.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:18, what does the author feel about his labor?
questions.explanation: The author states, 'I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun,' indicating a feeling of futility regarding his work.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 2:3 suggest about seeking pleasure?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:3 discusses the pursuit of pleasure and folly, indicating that seeking pleasure can lead to foolishness.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:6, what did the author make to water his trees?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees,' indicating his efforts in gardening.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 2:4 indicate about the author's accomplishments?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:4 states, 'I made me great works; I builded me houses,' showing his focus on accomplishments.

questions.question: True or False: The author in Ecclesiastes 2:10 found joy in his labor.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:10 states, 'for my heart rejoiced in all my labour,' indicating he found joy in his work.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ecclesiastes 2:11, the author's labor provided profit under the sun.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'and there was no profit under the sun,' indicating that his labor did not yield profit.

questions.question: True or False: The author believed that wisdom and folly have different outcomes according to Ecclesiastes 2:13.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:13 states that 'wisdom excelleth folly,' indicating a different valuation but not necessarily different outcomes.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:19, what is uncertain about the man who inherits the labor of another?
options: Whether he shall be a wise man or a fool
Whether he shall inherit gold or silver
Whether he shall build houses or plant vineyards
Whether he shall rejoice in his labor
questions.correctAnswer: Whether he shall be a wise man or a fool
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:19 states 'And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour,' showing the uncertainty about the inheritor's wisdom.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 2:20, what does the author say he did to his heart concerning all the labor he took under the sun?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:20 says 'Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun,' indicating the author's despair over his labor.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 2:21 identify as a 'great evil'?
options: Leaving labor done in wisdom to one who has not labored
questions.correctAnswer: Leaving labor done in wisdom to one who has not labored
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:21 states 'yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it for his portion. This also is vanity and a great evil,' describing the injustice of inheritance.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 2:22 asks, 'For what hath man of all his labour?' What is the answer given?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:22 says 'For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?' highlighting the frustration despite labor.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 2:24 say is the best thing for a man?
options: To eat and drink and enjoy good in his labor
To build houses and plant vineyards
questions.correctAnswer: To eat and drink and enjoy good in his labor
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:24 states 'There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour,' emphasizing enjoyment from labor.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 2:26, what does God give to the man who is good in His sight?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:26 says 'For God giveth to a man that is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy,' indicating God's blessing on the righteous.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'hebel' (הֶבֶל) as used in Ecclesiastes 2:1 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'hebel' (הֶבֶל) appearing in Ecclesiastes 2:1 is traditionally translated as 'vanity' or 'vapor,' indicating something fleeting or meaningless.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Ecclesiastes 2:11 to emphasize the futility of labor?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:11 uses inclusio by starting and ending with the theme of 'vanity and vexation of spirit,' framing the reflection on labor's futility.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of the vanity of labor and earthly pursuits found in Ecclesiastes 2:19-23?
questions.explanation: Matthew 6:19-21 warns against storing up treasures on earth, echoing Ecclesiastes 2:19-23's theme of the futility of labor that is ultimately left to others.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book shares a similar reflection on the fleeting nature of wisdom and labor as Ecclesiastes 2:12-16 does?
questions.explanation: The book of Job, like Ecclesiastes 2:12-16, grapples with the meaning of wisdom and the human condition, reflecting on life's seeming futility.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Ecclesiastes 2:19 in the text?
options: Verses about hating life due to the vanity of labor
Description of building houses and planting vineyards
The pursuit of wine and folly
The declaration of wisdom excelling folly
questions.correctAnswer: Verses about hating life due to the vanity of labor
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:17-18 immediately precede 2:19 and express hatred for life because of the grievous vanity of labor, setting the tone for 2:19.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 2:25, the phrase 'who can eat, or who else can hasten hereunto, more than I?' implies what about the author's perspective?
options: His unique ability to enjoy life's simple pleasures
questions.correctAnswer: His unique ability to enjoy life's simple pleasures
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:25 highlights the author's recognition that no one can enjoy eating and drinking more than he can, showing appreciation of simple joys.

questions.question: What literary technique is illustrated by the repetition of 'This is also vanity' throughout Ecclesiastes 2:19-26?
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase 'This is also vanity' serves as a refrain emphasizing the theme of meaninglessness in the passage.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 2:23 describes a man's days as 'sorrows' and his travail as 'grief.' How does this relate to the overall theme of the chapter?
options: It underscores the futility and burden of labor under the sun
It encourages joyful labor and reward
It contrasts wisdom and folly directly
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores the futility and burden of labor under the sun
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:23 emphasizes the sorrow and grief involved in labor, reinforcing the chapter's theme of life's vanity and frustration.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 2:26 states that God gives joy to the sinner to encourage repentance.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:26 says God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the man good in His sight, but to the sinner He gives travail; thus, the statement is false.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ecclesiastes 2:1 teach about human sin and pleasure?
options: Human pleasure apart from God is ultimately vanity
Sin leads to eternal separation from God
Pleasure is the highest good given by God
questions.correctAnswer: Human pleasure apart from God is ultimately vanity
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:1 states that pursuing mirth and pleasure is also vanity, teaching that such pursuits apart from God are ultimately meaningless.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ecclesiastes 2:13 teach about wisdom compared to folly?
options: Wisdom is superior to folly as light is superior to darkness
Folly is necessary for human growth
Wisdom and folly are equally valuable in God's plan
Folly surpasses wisdom in divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is superior to folly as light is superior to darkness
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:13 explicitly states that wisdom excels folly as light excels darkness, emphasizing the superiority of wisdom.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ecclesiastes 2:24 teach about sanctification and joy in labor?
options: Joy in one’s labor is a gift from God and the best good for man
Sanctification is achieved through asceticism and denial of pleasure
True joy is only found in eternal life, not earthly work
questions.correctAnswer: Joy in one’s labor is a gift from God and the best good for man
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:24 teaches that enjoying the fruits of one’s labor is good and comes from God, revealing a doctrine of sanctified joy in earthly work.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse Ecclesiastes 2:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:26 shows God's justice in giving wisdom and joy to the good, and travail to sinners, demonstrating His just governance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse Ecclesiastes 2:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Ecclesiastes 2:11, the author’s reflection on all his works as vanity indicates God's omniscience in revealing the true value of human endeavors.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 2:17 connect to the broader biblical theme of the problem of evil and human suffering?
options: It expresses the anguish caused by the vanity and futility of life under sin
It denies the existence of suffering
It teaches prosperity guarantees divine blessing
It affirms that suffering is always punishment for sin
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses the anguish caused by the vanity and futility of life under sin
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:17 reflects the grief and despair over life’s vanity, tying into biblical themes of human suffering due to the Fall.

questions.question: In what way does Ecclesiastes 2:18–19 prepare for New Testament teachings on inheritance and stewardship?
options: It highlights the uncertainty of earthly inheritance and human stewardship
It promises that all earthly labor will be rewarded to descendants
It denies the value of stewardship
It teaches that only the wise can inherit
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the uncertainty of earthly inheritance and human stewardship
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:18–19 emphasizes the vanity and uncertainty in leaving labor to others, prefiguring New Testament calls for faithful stewardship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ecclesiastes 2:13 and Ecclesiastes 2:14 teach about wisdom and human equality in death?
options: Wisdom excels folly in life but all share the same fate in death
Wisdom guarantees eternal life while folly leads to death
Folly surpasses wisdom because all die
Death discriminates between the wise and the fool
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom excels folly in life but all share the same fate in death
questions.explanation: Verse 2:13 emphasizes wisdom’s superiority, while 2:14 shows both wise and fool share the same death, teaching both the value of wisdom and human mortality.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ecclesiastes 2:21 and Ecclesiastes 2:22 teach about human labor and its ultimate value?
options: Human labor is often futile and may be inherited by those who did not labor
Labor is always rewarded in this life
Only the laborer benefits from his work
questions.correctAnswer: Human labor is often futile and may be inherited by those who did not labor
questions.explanation: Verses 2:21–22 reveal the vanity and injustice of labor being left to others who may not appreciate it, underscoring human futility under the sun.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ecclesiastes 2:24 and Ecclesiastes 2:26 teach about God’s provision and the gift of joy?
options: God grants joy and satisfaction in labor to the righteous as a gift
Joy is independent of God’s will
Only sinners receive joy in their labor
God’s provision is limited to material wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God grants joy and satisfaction in labor to the righteous as a gift
questions.explanation: Verse 2:24 states joy in labor is from God, and 2:26 shows God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to those good in His sight, teaching divine provision of joy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ecclesiastes 2:11-17 teaches life is utterly meaningless and hopeless. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Life under the sun without God’s perspective is vanity and vexation of spirit
Life is utterly meaningless and has no purpose whatsoever
Human wisdom guarantees escape from vanity
Death nullifies any need for moral living
questions.correctAnswer: Life under the sun without God’s perspective is vanity and vexation of spirit
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:11-17 laments vanity and vexation of spirit in earthly life, emphasizing the futility of human efforts apart from divine perspective, not total nihilism.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ecclesiastes 2:3 teach about the limits of human wisdom in relation to folly?
options: Human wisdom seeks to understand folly but finds ultimate meaning elusive
Human wisdom fully comprehends all aspects of life
Folly is superior to wisdom in understanding life
Wisdom negates any experience of folly
questions.correctAnswer: Human wisdom seeks to understand folly but finds ultimate meaning elusive
questions.explanation: Verse 2:3 shows the author acquainting his heart with wisdom and folly to seek meaning, revealing human wisdom’s limits in grasping life’s purpose.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ecclesiastes 2:26 reveal through the distribution of wisdom, joy, and travail?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:26 shows God’s providence in giving wisdom and joy to the good and travail to sinners, governing all circumstances.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 2:12-15 fit within the biblical narrative of human wisdom and its limits?
options: It acknowledges wisdom’s value but shows that it cannot prevent death or ultimate vanity
It denies any value to wisdom
It claims fools are wiser than the wise
questions.correctAnswer: It acknowledges wisdom’s value but shows that it cannot prevent death or ultimate vanity
questions.explanation: Verses 2:12-15 affirm wisdom’s excellence but also that both wise and fools share death, illustrating wisdom’s limits in human existence.

questions.question: What doctrine do Ecclesiastes 2:20-23 teach about despair and the human condition under sin?
options: Despair arises from labor’s futility and the restless heart under sin
Despair is unwarranted because all labor bears fruit
The human heart finds rest apart from God
questions.correctAnswer: Despair arises from labor’s futility and the restless heart under sin
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 2:20-23 describes the author’s despair over futile labor and restless sorrow, highlighting the human condition under sin’s curse.
